subject: Region-specific erase & authorization flow — roadmap ask
messages:
From: Sofia Trivedi <sofia.trivedi@finvault.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Data erasure by region / authorization flow (FinVault ask)

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We finished a compliance review with our legal and ops teams and have two related asks before we can sign up Dedicated capacity:

1) Ability to trigger customer-initiated erasure requests that only remove data from a specific region (e.g., purge EU shards but retain US for operational continuity), and

2) An auditable approval/authorization flow for cross-region erase requests (so our security team can approve or deny and we have an immutable log).

We already saw Redwood’s tenant-level retention controls in the console, but we need finer-grained controls (per-workspace or per-bucket within a tenant) and an approval step for some classes of requests. Attached is a brief matrix of our expected retention categories.

Can you map this to your roadmap and tell us the earliest timeline for a compliance-grade implementation? Also: will this feature be available for Dedicated customers or only in Redwood Private?

Best,
Sofia
Sofia Trivedi
Head of Compliance, FinVault
sofia.trivedi@finvault.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Trivedi <sofia.trivedi@finvault.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Aug 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data erasure by region / authorization flow (FinVault ask)

Hi Sofia —

Really helpful matrix, thanks for sharing. Short answer: we can cover this, but it’s a multi-layer deliverable and we want to be explicit about scope so we don’t underdeliver.

High-level mapping (subject to engineering validation):
- Phase 1 (MVP, Q4): Tenant-level and workspace-level retention flags with manual region purge APIs. These allow a customer admin to request erasure scoped to a region and workspace.
- Phase 2 (Q1 next year): Approval workflow + audit ledger tied to our Console and Private control plane. This includes role-based approvals and a signed audit record for each erase action.
- Phase 3: Fine-grained policies (per-bucket, per-model) and policy-driven automatic erasures plus cross-region dependency checks.

Two quick clarifications we need from FinVault: which classes of data must be region-only erasable (tokens/embeddings/raw transcripts), and whether you require a hard window (e.g., 30 days to approve) before a cross-region purge can execute.

For your question about Dedicated vs Private: Phase 1 can be shipped to Dedicated customers as an opt-in capability (we’ll still route the erasure operations within their reserved pools). Phases 2+ will have stronger guarantees and will be prioritized for Private deployments (due to immutability/audit log storage constraints), but we’ll backport a lightweight approval UI for Dedicated if needed.

Looping in Karthik and Laura to validate engineering effort and compliance implications.

Next steps: Karthik/Laura — can you give a rough estimate and call out any blockers? Jordan

--
Jordan Blake
Director, GTM Solutions @ Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Sofia Trivedi <sofia.trivedi@finvault.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2027 11:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data erasure by region / authorization flow (FinVault ask)

Thanks, Jordan / Sofia —

Engineering read: this is feasible but has three non-trivial elements that affect timeline and implementation approach:

1) Storage topology awareness — we need tagging at write time so that each object stores region residency metadata (if not already present). That’s ~2-3 sprints to audit and retrofit for older stores.

2) Safe purge primitives — an erase API that can remove data from a shard/region without violating cross-shard references. For some models, embeddings and KV caches reference tokens across regions; we’d need a conservative garbage-collection pass. Estimate: MVP 4–6 weeks of focused work plus safety tests.

3) Audit & authorization service — we can build an ACL-backed approval flow and append-only ledger. But to meet ‘‘audit-grade’’ requirements (tamper-evident, exportable for SOC2), we must choose storage (immutable append-only bucket vs vendor HSM signing). This is a design decision; depending on approach, effort varies widely.

Proposed timeline (tentative):
- Week 0–4: Design and data tagging plan; align on classes of data (Sofia to confirm).
- Week 4–10: Implement region-scoped purge API and console hooks (MVP).
- Week 10–18: Authorization service + audit ledger prototype.

Blockers / questions:
- Sofia: please confirm data categories and whether FinVault needs cross-region rollback capability.
- Laura: any constraints from security/audit we should bake into the design?

I’ll file a scoped RFC this afternoon and link to INF-4821.

—Karthik
Product Lead, Infrastructure

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Sofia Trivedi <sofia.trivedi@finvault.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Aug 2027 15:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data erasure by region / authorization flow (FinVault ask)

Jordan / Karthik / Sofia —

Appreciate the summary. A few security notes and follow-up actions from my side:

- Immutable audit: we should use a signed append-only ledger stored in a dedicated Private bucket for customers that need tamper-evidence. For Dedicated, we will provide an exportable signed record but recommend Private for long-term retention of audit artifacts.

- Approval model: two-tier approval for high-impact purges (security+legal). Low-risk erasures (synthetic logs, test embeddings) can be self-service. Need to codify "high-impact" criteria.

- Operational safety: add a mandatory dry-run/report mode for cross-region purges that shows the objects to be affected before action. Admins must explicitly confirm.

Action items:
1) Sofia: send the data-category mapping and any legal hold exceptions. (Sofia replied previously with a matrix — please flag any items that cannot be purged).
2) Jordan / Karthik: accept RFC and include the dry-run and two-tier approval in scope.
3) I will draft the audit storage spec and preferred signing approach (HSM vs signed manifests) by next Friday.

If FinVault is comfortable, we’ll target the MVP purge API for Dedicated as an opt-in by late Q4 and start Phase 2 in Q1. Laura

--
